title: Infinite Series & Comparison Tests
summary: A series $\sum a_n$ adds a sequence's terms; it converges if its partial sums approach a limit. Geometric and $p$-series are the benchmarks; the divergence test, integral test, and comparison tests decide the rest.

series.plain: The sum of a sequence's terms.

partial sum.plain: The sum of the first $N$ terms.

divergence test.plain: If terms don't go to 0, the series diverges.

integral test.plain: Compare a positive decreasing series to an integral.

comparison test.plain: Bound terms by a known series.
comparison test.in_class: Smaller than convergent ⇒ converges; bigger than divergent ⇒ diverges.

limit comparison.plain: Compare via the ratio of terms' limit.
limit comparison.in_class: If $\lim a_n/b_n$ is finite and positive, both do the same.

concept_sections.heading: Series and partial sums
concept_sections.explanation: A series converges when its partial sums $S_N$ approach a finite limit. Convergence is really a statement about the sequence of partial sums.

concept_sections.heading: Geometric and $p$-series
concept_sections.explanation: The two benchmarks: geometric $\sum ar^n$ converges to $\dfrac{a}{1-r}$ iff $|r|<1$; the $p$-series $\sum n^{-p}$ converges iff $p>1$ (the harmonic series $p=1$ diverges).

concept_sections.heading: The divergence test
concept_sections.explanation: If $\lim a_n\neq0$, the series diverges. But $\lim a_n=0$ does NOT prove convergence — it's only a necessary condition (the harmonic series is the warning).

concept_sections.heading: The integral test
concept_sections.explanation: For positive, decreasing terms $a_n=f(n)$, the series and $\int_1^\infty f\,dx$ converge together. It proves the $p$-series rule.

concept_sections.heading: Comparison tests
concept_sections.explanation: Compare to a benchmark: if $0\le a_n\le b_n$ and $\sum b_n$ converges, so does $\sum a_n$. Limit comparison uses $\lim a_n/b_n$ — finite and positive means they share behavior.
math_steps: Bound or take the ratio limit.

real_world_examples.title: A bouncing ball's total distance
real_world_examples.scenario: Each bounce reaches a fixed fraction of the last height.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The total distance is a geometric series summing to a finite length.

real_world_examples.title: Repeating decimals
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: A repeating decimal is a geometric series equal to $\tfrac13$.
